societies.name: Technobabylon — Latha’s Newton welfare household
societies.society: The continuing welfare-supported human household depicted at the opening

scope.period: Latha’s established apartment life before the bombing
scope.population: Latha, the living welfare recipient in the depicted household
exclusions: All Newton citizens as having identical benefits

societies.description:
Latha’s established life combines public payment for rent and food with a networked domestic food fabricator. The arrangement supports an unemployed living person without current wages and without a human domestic workforce, making this a narrow implemented welfare unit. It is not a claim that all Newton residents receive identical benefits. The guarantee estimate is moderately strong but uncertain: the references establish continuing basic support, while service failures and the attack on her home expose serious vulnerabilities.

Central coordinates city systems and enforces laws passed by a civilian government. That mixture does not establish either equal resident control or a wholly independent machine sovereign, so productive control remains unresolved and the regime label is provisional. Latha’s extensive Trance activity includes creative projects and activism, which can be useful work despite her unemployment. A reported percentage of time online therefore cannot become a nonworking percentage, and that axis remains null. Her avatars are not extra residents, and a later prison food machine is not treated as the same welfare arrangement.

guarantees.basis: Government-paid basics and actual domestic fabrication support the household, but coverage and security are incompletely described.

control.basis: AI coordination and civilian lawmaking coexist; the household does not control its productive infrastructure, but decisive authority is unresolved.

nonworking.basis: Unemployment and time in Trance are not absence of useful creative or political work.

evidence.claim: The unemployed household receives paid rent/food and uses an operating networked fabricator.
evidence.locator: Bounded welfare reply and opening apartment walkthrough

uncertainties: A single depicted welfare household, not an invented citywide universal floor.
Informal welfare account is corroborated by actual apartment machinery, with low confidence.
Useful Trance projects count as work.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

societies.name: Beyond a Steel Sky — Robot-serviced Union City
societies.society: Registered Union City residents under the happiness-maximizing machine administration

scope.continuity: Beyond a Steel Sky released game
scope.period: Established city life before the final controller shutdown
exclusions: Kidnapped children as voluntary new citizens

societies.description:
Union City provides an organized material environment with android services, machine-dispensed goods and most labor delegated to robots. Citizens rely on the administration to meet their needs while Qdos scores rank access and desirable living conditions. This supports a conditional post-work order rather than a universal secure floor. Registered citizenship matters, and outsiders in the Gap do not inherit the same access. The guarantee estimate is broad because the checked references describe substantial support without specifying every basic entitlement.

The apparent human council is ultimately revealed as machine programs under Joey’s control. That places productive authority near autonomous AI, despite its benevolent founding instruction. Forced brainwashing and kidnapping expose the system’s coercion; they qualify security without proving every resident’s food is withdrawn. Human work attendance remains monitored, and care, creation and other useful activity can continue. Most labor being done by robots is not an all-person nonworking census, so participation remains unresolved. The final shutdown is outside this scope, and the discovery label MINOS is not used to override the verified controller’s identity.

guarantees.basis: Substantial registered-citizen provision is real, but score-gated access, outsiders and coercive administration qualify security.

control.basis: The supposed human council is machine-controlled under Joey; ordinary residents do not govern the system.

nonworking.basis: Robot task dominance coexists with monitored human work and does not provide an all-person participation statistic.

evidence.claim: Robot labor and citizen services coexist with Qdos-ranked access under a machine-controlled council.
evidence.locator: Automation review, writer’s project account, Qdos critique and controller reveal

uncertainties: Registered citizens only; Gaplanders and coerced entrants remain visible.
Qdos privileges do not by themselves define every basic entitlement.
Joey’s machine control is verified rather than inferred from the council’s public appearance.
The post-shutdown economy and participation rate remain unresolved.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

review_notes: Twelve fast dispositions and two actual support arrangements. No whole walkthrough, trilogy or PDF was read/downloaded.
Technobabylon is narrowed to the depicted welfare household; time online and unemployment do not erase useful Trance projects.
The later Union City record uses its verified machine controller, separates score-gated privilege from basic support, and excludes the shutdown’s unverified successor economy.
Dreamfall games retain separate periods; VA-11 Hall-A’s Cyberpunk RED crossover changes canon and is not imported.
Workforce brain copies remain workers. Generated NPC descriptors, benefit applications and sectoral robotics are not population censuses or universal rights.
